predecessors.name: Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia
predecessors.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, which 'declared independence on 3 March 1992' (infobox 'Independence from Yugoslavia: 3 March 1992')

ledger.x: 1992-03: Bosnia and Herzegovina declares independence from Yugoslavia.
1992-04: the Bosnian War begins and the Serbs take most of the country.

1992-10: the Croat-Bosniak War begins; Croats and Bosniaks fight over Herzegovina and central Bosnia, and 'in early 1993 the Croat-Bosniak War escalated'; Herzeg-Bosnia was declared a republic on 28 August 1993.
1994-03: the Washington Agreement ends the Croat-Bosniak war.
1994-03: Herzeg-Bosnia's land passes to the new Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
1995-12: the Dayton Agreement is signed in Paris and Republika Srpska becomes an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
1995-12: after Dayton the official name becomes Bosnia and Herzegovina.

wars.name: Bosnian War
wars.outcome: Ended 21 November 1995 with the initialling of the Dayton Accords (signed in Paris on 14 December): the republic keeps its international borders and is divided into the Federation (51%) and Republika Srpska (49%); Herzeg-Bosnia is abolished in 1996.

wars.name: Croat-Bosniak War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Washington Agreement of March 1994, which joined Herzeg-Bosnia with the Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

certainty.note: The front lines of the Bosnian War are approximate and the pages give none year by year; the external frontier is the former republic boundary with Croatia and Serbia-Montenegro and was not changed.
